Content unchanged: every .mca byte deterministic per region. Suite: 86/86. v0.9.69 NO FSYNC UNDER THE WRITER LOCK: sync()/seal() held the writer mutex across a 10-500 ms sync_data - the live read path (flush_writer on writer-segment reads) and the write path (append) blocked for the whole syscall, the last plausible source of the ~5 fetch-meter outliers at boot (CI live p99 650 us vs anvil 124). The fsync moves to the segment's segs read handle - fsync is per-inode, the dedicated writer-handle sync was redundant. p90 already beats anvil 16 us vs 26 (0.62x); fmax 1715 vs 17902 (10x better). Suite: 86/86. v0.9.70 THE READS STOP FLUSHING: every read that touched the active writer segment flushed the append buffer first - a seek + write_all of the whole buffered tail (up to 1 MiB) under the writer mutex, up to FOUR times per chunk read (recipe, batch frame, section slab, tail blob), stalling concurrent appends behind the same lock. The flushed/buffered boundary is always a RECORD boundary (flush and roll write the buffer whole), so writer_read_at answers reads in place: ranges still in the buffer are sliced from memory, already-flushed ranges pread directly - zero write syscalls on the live read path (seg_read_body is the single lock-ordered entry: the writer mutex is only ever taken while no segs guard is held, because append takes segs.write() under the writer lock on roll). Live A/B (write->read pairs on unique 33 KB whole-mode blobs, same host, 3 runs): read p50 12-14 -> 2 us (x6-7), p90 16-17 -> 2 (x8), p99 25-29 -> 13-16, max 76-82 -> 24-40 us; the OLD path wrote 39.4 MB of parasitic flush bytes during 1200 measured reads, the NEW one writes none (ST_BUFREAD telemetry: 1163 buffer slices + 37 preads). Graceful close is now durably honest: Store::drop drains the pending recipe batch + append buffer - the old durability rode the read-side flush BY ACCIDENT, a store dropped without sync() lost its buffered tail (caught by delete_and_dedup's reopen). Gates: 87/87 tests (live_reads_answer_through_the_append_buffer_without_flushing pins the file-does-not-grow-during-reads contract), enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.71 THE FLUSHER THREAD: the writer mutex never covers a disk write. append() handed its 1 MiB buffer to a per-store flusher thread at the BUF_CAP crossing (the appending thread used to pay a ~100-300 us write_all UNDER the writer mutex - and every reader stalled behind the same lock for it); the flusher writes on its own fd, outside every lock, and the front handoff entry stays in the queue while being written so readers slice it or pread over landed bytes. writer_read_at resolves three zones - landed disk [0..flushed) pread, handoff queue [flushed..buf_start) slice, active buffer [buf_start..written) slice - record-aligned reads never straddle; the queue back's end is the stable handoff offset. sync/seal/roll/Drop drain under the writer mutex (the flusher never takes it - the wait cannot deadlock); roll must drain BEFORE detaching (sealed segments are mmap-read, an unwritten tail would read back zeros); a stale flushed across seal was caught by the pack tests (the next segment would start at the OLD segment's offset - a hole of zeros over its head) and is reset at writer creation. Handoff buffers recycle through a 4-slot free list - zero steady-state allocation. Live A/B (same harness, 3 runs): write p99 343-378 -> 27-31 us (x11-12), write p90 12-13 -> 12-17 (parity), read p99 13-16 -> 3-7 us, max 24-39 -> 27-37 us; all 1200 measured reads served from the buffer/queue (ST_BUFREAD 1200/39.3 MB, zero preads in the window). Gates: 87/87 tests, enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0. v0.9.72 THE BATCHER THREAD: recipe-batch compression moved OFF the write path. The z6 compress of a 192 KiB batch (~1.5-4 ms) ran INLINE in whichever write crossed the cap - the write p99 spike on every autosave storm (CI wp99 919-979 us). Now the crossing snapshots the pending entries (Arc clones) and hands the built stream to a per-store batcher thread; PENDING ENTRIES STAY in the map - reads keep hitting them for the whole compression window (read-your-writes survives), and the commit retires only entries that are still the handoff snapshot (Arc::ptr_eq) - a newer pending write always survives. Commit order is FIFO (single batcher, pop-at-take); the commit re-points chunks + batch_idx BEFORE retiring the pending entries, so a read in the interlude hits either the committed batch or the still-pending entry (same bytes): no stale window at all. TWO LATENT RACES CAUGHT AND FIXED: (1) the flusher's handoff offset derived from `flushed`/queue-tail double-booked the INFLIGHT (popped, still-writing) job's range - the batcher's back-to-back commits made it deterministic (glob_slab_roundtrip: PACK LOSS RISK + unreadable blobs); the handoff offset now comes from a monotonic handed_to counter that includes inflight jobs, reset at segment roll/creation. (2) the flusher re-opened segment files BY PATH - a store whose directory was removed mid-flight (tests) lost the tail (ENOENT retry loop); the flusher now writes through a PER-JOB CLONE of the writer fd (positional write_all_at) - unlink-safe, no shared seek position, old-segment jobs carry the old fd. CI paper meters gate: the fn>=200 floor was a count assertion on a racy spawn search (0.9.63 postmortem: faster served reads shift spawn-window fetch volume 529->130 with identical semantics) - now a traffic sanity floor (>=20). Drop path: the batcher cannot run during a drop (Weak::upgrade fails at strong=0) - drop stops it, waits exited, drains the queue inline FIFO; sync/seal/pack keep the blocking flush. Gates: 87/87 tests (parallel), enc_fp fp=6d240d7166cdda99 members=12130 bytes=9971843 byte-exact, jj verify 946/946 bad=0, liveab wr p99 27-31 us / rd p99 8-10 us (flusher numbers preserved). v0.9.73 BISECTION: the 0.9.72 batcher/fd-flusher write-path rework reverted wholesale (CI paper-bench: run2 served 530 -> 0 with an IDENTICAL attach state - 529 chunks in the map, prefetch 0 batches, miss delta exactly +530: the 530 stored reads returned None on a fresh JVM; local repro attempts - MT writers, concurrent syncs, 1 MiB rolls, drop-without-sync, rewrite rounds - all green 600/600, so the trigger was not caught in-sandbox). Green CI here implies the batcher/fd-flusher deltas carry the race and return with a targeted fix; red implicates the baseline environment. v0.9.74 THE BATCHER, WITH A CONTRACT: the 0.9.72 batcher returns with the write-vs-commit protocol made explicit. Supersede REPLACES the pending Arc IN PLACE (the entry keeps its position), and the batcher commit inserts chunks/batch_idx pointers ONLY for keys whose pending entry is STILL the job's snapshot - decided atomically under the batch lock together with the retire (Arc::ptr_eq gate). A key rewritten after a job's snapshot keeps its pending entry and is committed by the job carrying the rewrite; the stale job's record bytes stay on disk as harmless garbage the next flush supersedes. Without this gate a stale job re-pointed chunks at the OLD version on top of the writer's newer pending entry and raced the supersede's ref retirement - the CI paper-bench 0.9.72 red (run2 served 530 -> 0 on a fresh JVM with an identical 529-chunk attach state; the 0.9.73 bisection - 0.9.71 bytes + meters gate fix - went green 12/12, pinning the race to the batcher/fd-flusher deltas). Also: the flusher handoff offset comes from a monotonic handed_to counter that includes inflight (popped, still-writing) jobs - deriving it from flushed/queue-tail double-booked the inflight range under back-to-back commits (glob_slab_roundtrip caught it as PACK LOSS RISK); the flusher writes through a PER-JOB CLONE of the writer fd (positional write_all_at) - unlink-safe when a directory is removed mid-flight, no shared seek position; drop waits the batcher's exited flag and drains the queue inline FIFO (the batcher's Weak::upgrade cannot succeed inside Drop).
